Data and analysis from Census 2021

Retail sales rose in the three months to October 2026, according to our first estimate.

This is the latest release.
                View previous releases

Contact: Email Retail Sales team

Print this 
Statistical bulletin

The quantity of goods bought (volume) in retail sales is estimated to have risen by 0.4% in the three months to October 2026, compared with the three months to July 2026. Volumes rose for food stores, while fuel retailers mostly recovered from a fall in the three months to July following a spike in March.

Retail sales volumes are estimated to have risen by 0.7% in October 2026. This follows a fall of 0.6% in September 2026 (revised down from a 0.4% fall in our previous bulletin), and a rise of 0.8% in August 2026 (revised up from a 0.7% rise in our previous bulletin). Food stores sales volumes rose as supermarkets reported increased sales of long-life items such as tinned goods and UHT milk following government advice, while art galleries and clothing stores also rose on the month.

Sales volumes rose over both the month and the three months to October 2026

Sales volumes rose by 0.4% in the three months to October 2026, compared with the three months to July 2026.

Food stores rose as supermarkets reported an October uplift on emergency items such as UHT milk and tinned goods following the launch of the UK government's Be Ready campaign on 22 October 2026. Meanwhile, specialist food stores such as butchers and bakers reported strong sales volumes in September.

Fuel sales were low in May and June after a spike in sales in March following the outbreak of the conflict in the Middle East, but have since recovered gradually. As a result, sales volumes rose over the three months to October 2026.

Total sales volumes (including automotive fuel) rose by 0.7% over the month to October 2026. Supermarket sales rose following lower clothing sales in September, with October further helped by the boost in long-life food items.

Non-food stores sales volumes (the total of department, clothing, household, and other non-food stores) rose by 1.1% on the month. Other non-food stores were boosted by rises for art galleries, following a quiet September, and sports equipment, games and toy stores. Clothing store sales also rose, which retailers attributed to people buying more per visit, new launches and increased stock following inventory issues in September.

Within non-store retail, volumes partially recovered after a fall in September, with online clothing retailers commenting that the more autumnal October weather supported sales. This followed reports in September that the release of autumn and winter ranges suffered during the unseasonably warm weather.

However, automotive fuel volumes fell back to August levels as prices rose for the third consecutive month.

Online sales rose over both the month and the three months to October 2026

The amount spent online, known as "online spending values", rose by 1.6% in the three months to October 2026 compared with the three months to July 2026. Online spending values rose by 8.9% when compared with the three months to October 2025.

Within the monthly series, online sales values rose by 1.5% in October 2026, up from a fall of 0.3% in September, and were 9.7% higher compared with October 2025.

The total spend (the sum of in-store and online sales) rose by 1.2% over the month. As a result, the proportion of sales made online rose from 29.1% in September 2026 to 29.2% in October 2026.

Retail Sales Index Dataset | Released 20 November 2026 A series of retail sales data for Great Britain in value and volume terms, seasonally and non-seasonally adjusted.

Retail sales pounds data Dataset | Released 20 November 2026 Total sales and average weekly spending estimates for each retail sector in Great Britain in thousands of pounds.

Retail Sales Index internet sales Dataset | Released 20 November 2026 Internet sales in Great Britain by store type, month, and year.

Retail Sales Index categories and their percentage weights Dataset | Released 27 March 2026 Retail sales categories and descriptions and their percentage of all retailing in Great Britain.

For October 2026, the Retail Sales Index (RSI) survey response rates were 57.5% based on returned forms, which is 1.8 percentage points below the average of the past 12 months. This accounted for 93.8% of total turnover coverage of the sample population, 5.8 percentage points above the average of the past 12 months. Historical response information is available in our Retail sales quality tables dataset.

Information on how we calculated the data, including strengths and limitations, and a glossary of relevant terms, is available in our Retail Sales Index quality and methodology information (QMI) report.

Seasonally adjusted estimates are derived by estimating and removing calendar effects (for example, Easter moving between March and April), and seasonal effects (for example, increased spending in December because of Christmas) from the non-seasonally adjusted estimates.

We use the X-13ARIMA-SEATS approach to seasonal adjustment. Seasonal adjustment parameters are monitored closely and are regularly reviewed. Improvements following our full annual seasonal adjustment review were last implemented as part of the June 2026 release. More information is available in our Seasonal adjustment methodology.

Seasonal adjustment is applied at the industry level, and the seasonally adjusted series are aggregated to create estimates by industry sector and total retail. As part of our quality assurance approach, residual seasonality checks are completed regularly by our time series analysis team on both the seasonally adjusted series and the indirectly derived aggregate time series.

Based on current data, we find no residual seasonality in the main aggregate for monthly retail sales estimates. We have separately published our comprehensive methodology on How the Office for National Statistics (ONS) assesses statistical outputs for residual seasonality.

These accredited official statistics were independently reviewed by the Office for Statistics Regulation in March 2015. They comply with the standards of trustworthiness, quality, and value in the Code of Practice for Statistics and should be labelled "accredited official statistics".

Office for National Statistics (ONS), released 20 November 2026, ONS website, statistical bulletin, Retail sales, Great Britain: October 2026
